sources.document: Caracteristicas Geodinamicas en el Distrito de Paita - Informe Tecnico N032-2021/IGP
admissible_claims: IGP identifies El Zanjon as the principal local ravine and Nueva Esperanza, La Piscina, Catarata and Villa Naval as named contributing ravines in the Paita urban setting
the study states that the named contributing ravines ultimately drain through the principal El Zanjon system to the Pacific in its generalized local-drainage description
the study is based on field inspection and identifies ravines that activate in rainy periods
forbidden_inferences: the generalized routing statement overrides more specific official routing for Villa Naval
the report supplies survey-grade child geometries or outlet coordinates
rainfall climatology in the report is an IRFEN activation threshold
generic rainy-period activation proves a dated child event

sources.institution: Municipalidad Provincial de Paita / CENEPRED SIGRID
sources.document: Plan de Prevencion y Reduccion del Riesgo de Desastres de la Provincia de Paita 2019-2021
admissible_claims: El Zanjon drains much of Paita Baja through a canal-way that reaches the sea and the plan reports overflow and widespread urban inundation during the 1983 El Nino event
La Piscina is described as draining toward El Zanjon
La Catarata is described as draining from Paita Alta toward El Zanjon
Villa Naval is described as draining toward the Rada del Complejo Pesquero, with possible diversion toward Puerto Nuevo under severe conditions
forbidden_inferences: the report proves 1983 activation of La Piscina, La Catarata or Villa Naval separately
Villa Naval may be forced into El Zanjon contrary to the more specific routing description
described insufficient section is a current quantified hydraulic capacity
return-period rainfall values in the plan are IRFEN thresholds
